findings.title: PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs is a top-churn monolith co-locating UI event handling, network orchestration, file I/O/backup-restore, artwork-selection invocation, panel/search navigation, bulk-operation loops, and library-operation guarding in one class
findings.why_it_matters: Top-churn file by roughly 5x (38 edits/6mo vs 8 for the next file); architecture_quality was stuck at 7.5 across 19 critic passes before loops 10-12 started landing sequenced slices out of it.
findings.what_is_wrong: PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs still mixes UI event handling, file I/O/backup-restore invocation, artwork-selection invocation, panel/search navigation, bulk-operation loops, and library-operation guarding after loops 10-12's extractions. This loop narrowed the panel/search navigation concern further: PopulateGridSelectionPanelAsync's grid/icon-combining and per-tile display-fallback decision logic is now GridSelectionItems.BuildOrdered, a pure, directly-tested function - leaving the method itself with only the session-staleness guard, the AppliedArtworkStore lookup, and the XAML-population loop.

findings.title: LoadGameEntriesAsync resolves each unmatched game's name and SteamGridDB match sequentially, one network round trip at a time, on every widget open
findings.why_it_matters: On a library with many unmatched games, the fully-sequential per-entry network chain adds latency that scales linearly with library size.
findings.what_is_wrong: GameMatchResolver.ResolveAsync's per-entry network sequence (SteamGridDB platform-ID lookup, store name-fetch, SteamGridDB name search) runs in strict sequence across entries, even though the awaits are independent across entries. Unchanged this loop.
evidence: SteamGridDB.Xbox/PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:426-697 (unchanged this loop - this loop's own edit is entirely inside PopulateGridSelectionPanelAsync, ~650 lines further down the file)
findings.why_weakens_submission: A real, linearly-scaling latency cost, but BLOCKED: the recorded standing user constraint (no behavioural oracle for per-game network-call ordering/concurrency changes against SteamGridDB/GOG/Epic/Ubisoft) means this loop cannot land a change altering observable call ordering/concurrency/count without a product decision this loop cannot make.
findings.minimal_correction_path: BLOCKED this loop; named for continuity per Backlog Prioritization Pass criterion 0.

builder_notes.pattern: A loop executor can die mid-flight (infra failure, not a logic bug) after making real code changes but before any artifact records what happened.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: CURRENT_REVIEW.json.loop behind HEAD's own commit-message loop number, a dirty working tree with no LOOP_STATE.json, and no implementation-review verdict recorded anywhere.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Verify first (build + test + read), decide second (adopt or discard), commit third. Never skip straight to commit because the diff 'looks plausible.'
builder_notes.stack_example: C#: this loop re-ran msbuild and run-tests.ps1 from a clean invocation against the orphaned working tree before reading a single line of the new GridSelectionItems.cs, rather than assuming the prior executor's own (unrecorded) intent was sound.

builder_notes.pattern: The most specific F-022 candidate a backlog has ever named turned out to be exactly right, once someone (even an executor that then crashed) actually tried it.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A prior loop's minimal_correction_path names a specific method and a specific sub-piece of it (not just 'investigate panel navigation' generically) - that specificity is itself a signal the candidate is close to ready.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: When a backlog item narrows from 'investigate this whole area' to 'investigate this specific sub-decision inside this specific method,' treat that narrowing as progress worth trusting, not as a reason to re-litigate from scratch.
builder_notes.stack_example: C#: loop 12's own text named PopulateGridSelectionPanelAsync's list-construction specifically; this loop confirmed that exact sub-piece was both real (decision logic, not XAML shell) and extractable (six explicit inputs, one value-struct list out).

builder_notes.pattern: Fresh grep-based sweeps (not just re-reading the file linearly) surface duplication shapes a line-by-line read can miss.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Two or more XAML event-driven 'panels' or 'flows' in the same file, each with its own session/guard/focus-tracking fields declared side by side, and near-identical Show*/Hide* method bodies.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Before naming a decomposition candidate as 'done' or 'thin,' grep the file for the sibling of whatever you just extracted from rather than assuming symmetry has already been checked.
builder_notes.stack_example: C#: HideGridPanelAsync (~1543-1586) and HideSearchPanelAsync (~1788-1828) share the same guard-acquire/session-capture/animate-out/guard-release shape, byte-near-identical, not yet consolidated or extracted.

narrative: Place, not win. This loop's defining decision was procedural, not architectural: a prior executor died mid-flight after writing real, plausible-looking code with zero recorded verification, and this loop treated 'plausible-looking' as worthless without independently re-running the same gate any self-authored change would face - full build, full test suite, and a from-scratch read of both the new module and the method it came from. That verification held: the orphaned GridSelectionItems extraction is exactly the most specifically-named F-022 candidate any prior loop's backlog has produced, it is genuinely stateless and deletion-test-clean, and its 16 tests exercise real output rather than internal steps. architecture_quality moves up for the third time this run as a direct, source-backed consequence. test_strategy does not cross its own stated anchor this loop despite genuine new coverage, because the specific gap that has held it at 8.5 across three loops is untouched - an honest SAME rather than a generous nudge. The risk to watch for loop 14: this loop's own fresh sweep found the grid and search pickers independently maintain a near-identical four-field lifecycle-state quadruple, which is either the next real decomposition/dedup slice or a case where unifying two genuinely-different-enough things would trade real duplication for ceremony - loop 14 needs to prove friction fresh before committing to either read.
